readerQuestion: How can I send one Home Assistant notification to both household phones and keep it working when a phone is replaced?
directAnswer: Verify a plain message on each registered phone, create a Notify group helper containing those phone notify entities, and call notify.send_message on that group. Basic entity notifications carry message/title; use phone-specific actions or a YAML action group for advanced options or older installations. Rehearse with the inert toggle before using the group for everyday reminders and update membership when replacing a phone.
originalContribution: Section 4 provides a complete off-to-on practice-toggle automation and a five-trial recipient matrix that separates single-phone delivery, group membership and trigger behavior. Section 6 gives a phone-replacement acceptance procedure, including a freshly labeled message, checking the unchanged second phone and checking that a still-registered retired phone receives no new group message.
limitations: Documentation and tagged-source research, not physical-phone or Home Assistant runtime testing. Three YAML examples were parsed with duplicate-key rejection, but no real push messages were sent. Delivery time, receipt, read status and advanced Android/iOS payload compatibility were not measured. App menus vary by version. The conceptual cover does not depict a tested Tara installation.

claimChecks.claim: Mobile App gained notify entities in Home Assistant 2026.5 alongside existing phone-specific actions, allowing UI group helpers; the guide gives an older-installation fallback rather than assuming every installation has entities.

The Mobile App notify entity is created only when its registration supports push. Its entity method accepts message and optional title; advanced phone payloads stay on phone-specific actions. Verified in the tagged 2026.10.4 implementation.

Notify entity groups are created in the UI; notify action groups are configured in YAML. Action-group members use services entries with action names omitting notify.; the optional example follows the current documented shape.
notify.send_message targets one or more notify entities, with message required and title optional where supported. The guide targets one explicit group rather than assuming a household broadcast.
notify.notify selects the first notification action Home Assistant finds. A notify entity timestamp records last sent, not recipient acknowledgement or a read receipt.
A notify group remains available when any member is available; title support requires all members to support it. This is why group availability alone is not used as evidence of all-phone delivery.
The practice Toggle helper is a software on/off value with no attached hardware. Its explicit off-to-on trigger sends one practice message per qualifying transition; it has no repeating timer.
The complete example uses the documented trigger: state with from off/to on. Leaving the helper on is not a second state transition; manual Run actions does not verify that trigger.
Current Settings > Tools is available to administrators. Earlier releases use Developer tools; the article makes the menu/version difference and prerequisite explicit.
Plain tests must work on each phone before group diagnosis. Companion notification permission and registration are prerequisites; group creation does not repair a failed recipient path.

The optional YAML group belongs in configuration.yaml or its included notify list, not the automation editor. Validate changes before applying them, preserve a previous configuration copy and schedule a suitable restart.
Recipient grouping does not make delivery local-only. Local Push uses a separate WebSocket connection with platform-specific requirements instead of Apple/Google push infrastructure.

A notification button needs response handling. Sending an advanced payload to two phones does not by itself resolve conflicting replies; the article links to the established actionable-notification owner.
